title: Hera — Echoes in later ages
summary: Hera, queen of the gods, is goddess of marriage and family. This study traces the myth's afterlife.
body:
Hera, queen of the gods, is goddess of marriage and family. Her vengeful pursuit of Zeus's lovers fills many myths.

Long after its gods lost worshippers, Hera kept working — in Renaissance painting, in Romantic poetry, in modern film. Each age found its own anxieties reflected in the old story. Viewed through a symbolic lens, Hera is read for its images — what each figure and object stands for beneath the plot.

Myths survive by being reusable. Hera proved endlessly reusable. A second sub-question concerns the historical kernel: what real events or places might stand behind Hera. Related entries in this archive: Enuma Elish and Tanabata.
key_points: Afterlife of Hera through the centuries.
